Question ID: ENG1_U01_L03_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.R.10

Passage: The art teacher placed labeled bins near each table so students could return markers, scissors, and glue without crossing the room. The new system helped cleanup finish faster. Question: Which evidence best supports the paraphrase "The labeled bins made cleanup more efficient"?

answer.text: A. The room had tables.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This detail is true but does not prove that cleanup became more efficient.

answer.text: B. Students used markers.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This names one supply, but it does not explain how the bins helped cleanup.

answer.text: C. The art teacher placed labeled bins near each table.

feedback.text: Correct. This detail directly explains why students could clean up faster.

answer.text: D. Glue was one supply.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This detail is too small and does not support the paraphrase.

Question ID: ENG1_U01_L03_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.R.10

Passage: The soccer coach moved practice to the shaded field during the hottest week of the season. Players were able to complete drills with fewer heat breaks. Question: Which paraphrase is best supported by the passage?

answer.text: A. The players stopped practicing because the field was too shaded.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage says players completed drills, not that practice stopped.

answer.text: B. The coach canceled every drill during the hottest week.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage says players completed drills.

answer.text: C. The players asked to remove shade from the field.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage does not say players wanted less shade.

answer.text: D. The coach changed the practice location to help players work safely during hot weather.

feedback.text: Correct. This keeps the meaning and is supported by the shaded field and fewer heat breaks.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U01_L03_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.R.10

Passage: The club posted meeting reminders on the school website and near the front office. Attendance increased because students had more than one place to find the information. Question: Which evidence best supports the paraphrase "The reminders helped more students attend meetings"?

answer.text: A. The club had meetings.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not prove that reminders helped attendance.

answer.text: B. The front office was near the reminder.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This detail is about location, not the result.

answer.text: C. The school had a website.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is only one place where reminders were posted.

answer.text: D. Attendance increased.

feedback.text: Correct. This directly supports the idea that more students attended.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U01_L03_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.R.10

Passage: The library created a shelf for books recommended by students. The librarian said the shelf encouraged students to try books their classmates enjoyed. Question: Which explanation best connects the evidence to the paraphrase?

answer.text: A. The shelf was in the library, so the library had books.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain the purpose of student recommendations.

answer.text: B. Student recommendations helped classmates find books other students liked.

feedback.text: Correct. This connects the evidence to the paraphrase clearly.

answer.text: C. The librarian said something, so the shelf was not useful.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This contradicts the passage.

answer.text: D. The books were on a shelf, so students did not read them.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage says the shelf encouraged students to try books.

Question ID: ENG1_U01_L03_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.R.10

Passage: The science class used a clear jar to model erosion. When water was poured over the soil, students watched small pieces of dirt move away from the surface. Question: Which evidence best supports the paraphrase "The model showed how water can move soil"?

answer.text: A. Students watched small pieces of dirt move away from the surface.

feedback.text: Correct. This directly shows water moving soil.

answer.text: B. The class was a science class.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This gives the subject area but does not prove how water moved soil.

answer.text: C. The jar was clear.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This explains visibility, not the erosion process.

answer.text: D. The class used a jar.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The jar alone does not prove what the model showed.
